newsitem.title: SUDAN: U.N. food programme sends aid to southern Sudan.
newsitem.headline: U.N. food programme sends aid to southern Sudan.

text.p: The United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) said it sent a relief plane with food aid to the southern regional capital of Juba on Thursday.
Fighting in the area between southern rebels and Sudan government troops has deprived thousands of residents of food.
WFP country director Philip Clarke told Reuters the plane was loaded with 30 tonnes of food. He said WFP planned to airlift 200 more tonnes of food to Juba as soon as possible.
Barges loaded with 4,000 tonnes of food are slated to leave for Juba by April 16, he added.

"Around 2,325 tonnes of that food is meant for the people of Juba while the rest is to be distributed along the way in areas held both by the government and the rebel Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA)," Clarke said.
The government and SPLA rebels have told WFP they would allow the aid to pass through areas they control, he said.

Sudan on Sunday warned U.N. relief groups to stay away from areas in the south where its army was locked in battle with the SPLA. The rebel group has been fighting since 1983 for greater autonomy or independence for the Christian and animist south from the Moslem and Arabised north.
The SPLA seized Yei, 160 km (100 miles) southwest of Juba, on March 12 and vowed to continue to the more strategic Juba.
Travellers say there is very little food in Juba. They say the army has prevented residents from leaving to get food for security reasons. Both sides have mined the surrounding areas.

Clarke said the town's stores are empty because it has been deprived of relief for many months. Food scarcity has sent the price of staples rocketing in Juba, and residents say a sack of sorghum now costs 100,000 pounds ($66).

Before the war, the WFP distributed between 250 and 300 tonnes of relief food every month in Juba. Clarke said it would distribute the relief food to the old, handicapped, lactating mothers, children, refugees and the recently displaced.
The agency said over 8,300 displaced people and refugees had fled to Juba from Yei and Kajokaji since the SPLA captured them.
